Anyone want to talk about Finding Dory?

I liked it. I enjoyed how they linked to the first film by giving us a glimpse of Dory as a child and then skipping through time and we watch her grow up until she eventually bumps into Marlin at the beginning of the first film. The ending was cool and I thought that it was funny and ridiculous seeing how crazy Dory's on the spot thinking ended up creating complete chaos at the end. It made me laugh several times. I thought Marlin and Nemo were going to have more of a role in the film, but that was taken up by Hank with his ability to actually move through dry land. The reunion between Dory and her parents was touching and I really like how they got Dory to find her parents herself using something they've been hinting at almost the entire film. I honestly thought they were dead, but okay, they just were hanging out in the kelp near the institute.

There was a lot of flashbacks and I think they over used it. It really cut into the flow of the film and even in the most intense moments, the entire film just stops so Dory can remember five seconds of her childhood. I'm disappointed that Marlin and Nemo were basically useless and honestly, the entire film could have been done without them. There wasn't much to say about setting though. The Institute had only one visually stunning piece, but the rest was forgettable. It was mostly pipes and backrooms and nothing interesting like the previous film. There wasn't any one setting that sticks out.

I say it was a good film. Setting-wise and visually, it wasn't as good as the first film, but the story was better. The new characters they introduced were okay, but not really as memorable as the characters in the first film; I don't think anyone is going to be quoting them anytime soon.
